newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: P.Telecom, Telefonica link looks to South America.
newsitem.headline: P.Telecom, Telefonica link looks to South America.

text.p: The accord between Portugal Telecom and Spain's Telefonica is aimed at developing their interests in South America and Africa, government sources said.
"Both Latin America and Africa are developing markets where the prospects for growth are enormous," said one government source who declined to be identified.
A Portugal Telecom spokeswoman said on Tuesday that the company had reached an accord with its Iberian neighbour that would include a share exchange.
She declined to say what the level of the share swap would be or to give details of the accord which she said went well beyond a simple exchange of stock.
"It is easy to see that at stake here are communications around the Atlantic, between Europe and Africa and the whole of America," said another source linked to the process.
Portugal Telecom on Monday announced that it had chosen the Anglo-U.S. venture Concert -- made up of British Telecom and MCI -- as its global ally.
The new partners said that developing the Latin American market, where Portugal has historical links, would be one of the main aims of the alliance.
"Concert, through its alliance policies, wants to have a dominant position (there)," said one industry source.
MCI is already one of the major operators between the South and North American markets.

"Yesterday, when the minister spoke of a great Atlantic alliance is was not just a manner of speaking, he was talking about the prospects of a great alliance in the making," the government source said, referring to remarks by Planning Minister Joao Cravinho on Monday.

Most analysts believe that the developments of the past two days have reinforced speculation that Telefonica, which belongs to a rival international grouping, is about to jump ship and link up with Concert.
Telefonica is allied to the AT&T -led group Unisource.
